hints: Look at the name S phase. The S stands for synthesis, so ask yourself what is being made in the nucleus during this phase.
Remember that DNA replication doubles the DNA mass, but G2 is just a growth and checking gap with no further DNA synthesis.
walkthrough:
**Recall what happens in each stage**

Think of G1 as the normal starting cell with its usual amount of DNA. S phase is where DNA replication happens, so every chromosome is copied. G2 is just growth after copying, no more DNA is made.

Rule to remember: S phase doubles DNA, G2 keeps it the same.

**Calculate the mass at the end of S phase**

We start with $1.2 \times 10^{-12} \text{ g}$ in G1. Replication doubles it.

$$1.2 \times 10^{-12} \text{ g} \times 2 = 2.4 \times 10^{-12} \text{ g}$$

**Check the mass at the end of G2 phase**

Nothing is replicated in G2, the cell just grows and prepares for mitosis. So the mass stays at the doubled value.

End of S = $2.4 \times 10^{-12} \text{ g}$ and end of G2 = $2.4 \times 10^{-12} \text{ g}$, which matches option D.

options.A: This suggests no DNA replication happened at all, but S phase must double the DNA from G1.
options.B: This keeps S phase unchanged and only doubles in G2, but doubling happens in S, not in G2.
options.C: This correctly doubles DNA in S but then wrongly halves it in G2, and DNA is only halved at cell division, not in G2.
options.D: DNA doubles in S phase to 2.4 x 10-12 g and stays at that doubled mass through G2, ready for mitosis.
